JACQUEMUS TAKES SHANGHAI

With China set to represent 40% of global luxury consumption by 2030, the market offers unparalleled growth driven by young, digital-first consumers who live at the intersection of fashion, culture, and social commerce. Jacquemus, with its viral marketing edge, immersive storytelling, and lifestyle expansion, is uniquely positioned to capture this momentum and build lasting cultural relevance across platforms like WeChat, Tmall, and Xiaohongshu.


My strategy here lays out a 1–5 year roadmap for Jacquemus to enter and scale in China through experiential retail, cultural tailoring, and omnichannel commerce.

Year 2 & 3

Year 1

  • Following that year we would have pop-ups in Beijing & Chengdu, launch official Jacquemus RED (Xiaohongshu) account with behind-the-scenes & influencer collaborations
  • To start this expansion in the China marrket we propose opening a flagship store in Shanghai, with a WeChat & T-mall presence for Jacquemus.

Year 3 & 5

  • After that we would have boutiques around Beijing, localized brand collabs, add a Douyin flagship store Enable AR try-on features via WeChat Mini-Program and JD partnerships

The retail experience centers on an immersive Provençal-inspired flagship in Shanghai, designed to bring Jacquemus’s signature storytelling to life. Local artist collaborations weave French heritage with Chinese cultural elements, creating a space that feels both authentic and locally relevant. Seasonal exclusives further amplify excitement, using hype and scarcity to draw consumers in and position the flagship as a must-visit destination for China’s luxury audience.


This project taught me how distribution intersects with culture and consumer behavior. I learned how omnichannel tools, when localized, build loyalty and help luxury brands thrive in new markets.
